definitions.explanation: A formal religious ceremony or festival, typically associated with Shinto shrines or Buddhist temples. More formal and solemn in tone than the everyday word 祭り.

examples.japanese: {神社|じんじゃ}で{祭礼|さいれい}が{行|おこな}われた。
examples.english: A religious ceremony was held at the shrine.

examples.japanese: この{祭礼|さいれい}は{毎年|まいとし}{秋|あき}に{開催|かいさい}される。
examples.english: This festival is held every autumn.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}くから{伝|つた}わる{祭礼|さいれい}には、{地域|ちいき}の{人々|ひとびと}が{大勢|おおぜい}{参加|さんか}する。
examples.english: Many local people participate in the traditional festival that has been passed down for generations.

notes:
Compound of {祭|さい} (festival, worship) and {礼|れい} (ceremony, rite). A formal term that emphasizes the religious and ceremonial aspects of a festival, as opposed to the celebratory or entertainment aspects.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {祭|まつ}り — festival; the everyday, broad term covering both religious and secular events
- {儀式|ぎしき} — ceremony; ritual; more general, not limited to festivals
- {神事|しんじ} — Shinto ritual; specifically religious, not the public celebration
- {例祭|れいさい} — regular festival; the main annual festival of a shrine

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {祭礼|さいれい}を{行|おこな}う — to hold a religious festival
- {祭礼|さいれい}に{参加|さんか}する — to participate in a festival
- {伝統的|でんとうてき}な{祭礼|さいれい} — traditional religious festival
- {秋|あき}の{祭礼|さいれい} — autumn festival

REGISTER:
Formal and written. In everyday conversation, {祭|まつ}り or お{祭|まつ}り is much more common.
